Effective 1 July 2025, a 6% Service Tax will be imposed on non-Malaysian citizens, applicable to all fees and charges, except International Security Deposit and EMGS application fees. Fees shown in the Fee Schedule are exclusive of the 6% Service Tax. The Service Tax rate and taxable fee components are subject to change as determined by government regulations.

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: Entry Requirements Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? Our programme offers an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about the field of Information Technology. To ensure a smooth admission process, please take note of our entry requirements listed below. Prerequisites SPM/O-Level with Pre-University/Foundation Pass SPM/O-level or equivalent with 5 credits (including Mathematics) for entry with Pre-U/Foundation qualification (Except for UEC). SPM/O-Level with Diploma Pass SPM/O-level or equivalent with 3 credits (including Mathematics) for entry with Diploma qualification. Note: Candidates without a credit in mathematics at SPM level or its equivalent may be admitted if the STPM (Pre-U) / Matriculation / Foundation / Diploma in Computer Science or Software Engineering or Information Technology or Information System or Science and Technology or Business Studies programme contains subjects in mathematics that are equivalent or higher to mathematics at SPM level. Candidates without a credit in Mathematics at SPM level/equivalent or without a subject in Mathematics at a higher level, need to take and pass the reinforcement Mathematics subject that is equivalent to the SPM level. The reinforcement Mathematics subject must be offered in the first semester or before enrolment with unconditional offer. Reinforcement Mathematics can be offered as part of or outside the curriculum structure. If Reinforcement Mathematics is offered as part of the curriculum structure, it should count as an addition to the total number of credits required for graduation. Note : Candidates without a credit in Mathematics at SPM level/equivalent or without a subject in Mathematics at a higher level, need to take a reinforcement Mathematics with appropriate topics in the discipline of Information Technology and Information Systems at the beginning of the study. All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university. Entry Pathway AUSMAT (SACEi) Min. ATAR 55 A Level Min. DD Canadian Pre-University (CPU) Min. average of 55% in 6 subjects Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) Min. Grade C in at least 2 subjects Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) Pass with minimum 5Bs, including Mathematics or Advanced Mathematics or Adv. Mathematics 1 or 2 (Note: Candidates without a Grade ‘B’ in UEC subjects above may be admitted if the candidate has a credit in Mathematics at SPM or equivalent) Foundation Pass Foundation with CGPA 2.0 Diploma in Information Technology (DIT) Taylor's Diploma in IT with min. CGPA 2.50 (candidates with CGPA below 2.50 but above 2.00 may be admitted subject to thorough rigorous assessment) (Pre-requisite of Credit in Mathematics at SPM level or equivalent is not required) International Baccalaureate (IB) Min. 24 points in 6 subjects Monash University Foundation Year (MUFY) Overall 50% Other Qualifications Diploma in Computing (Level 4, MQF) or equivalent with a minimum CGPA of 2.50. Candidates with a CGPA below 2.50 but more than 2.00 may be admitted subject to a thorough rigorous assessment; (Pre-requisite of Credit in Mathematics at SPM level or equivalent is not required) Any other Diploma (Level 4, MQF) with a minimum CGPA of 2.75. Candidates with a CGPA below 2.75 but more than 2.50 can be admitted subject to a thorough rigorous assessment; Pass High School Certificate from New South Wales, Australia with an average of 60% Pass ANY Foundation with min CGPA 2.0 from other institutions recognized by the Malaysian Government Pass Matriculation programs recognized by the Ministry of Education Malaysia in the relevant field with min CGPA 2.00 Diploma Kemahiran Malaysia (DKM) / Diploma Vokasional Malaysia (DVM) / Diploma Lanjutan Kemahiran Malaysia (DLKM) in Computing fields with a minimum CGPA of 2.50 subjected to HEP Senate / Academic Board’s approval; Any other qualifications are recognised as equivalent by the Malaysia Government. Application via APEL A is allowed. Notes : Candidates without a credit in mathematics at SPM level or its equivalent may be admitted if the STPM (Pre-U) / Matriculation / Foundation Diploma in Computer Science or Software Engineering or Information Technology or Information System or Science and Technology or Business Studies programme contains subjects in mathematics that are equivalent or higher to mathematics at SPM level. Candidates without a credit in Mathematics at SPM level/equivalent or without a subject in Mathematics at a higher level, need to take a reinforcement Mathematics with appropriate topics in the discipline of Information Technology and Information Systems at the beginning of the study All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.

description.en: The Bachelor of Information Technology (Honours) at Taylor’s University prepares you to manage, design, and support modern computer systems across a wide range of industries. You will build strong technical expertise in both hardware and software, gaining a solid foundation in software development, systems networks, cybersecurity, and database management systems. Our curriculum moves beyond simply writing computer programmes to place strong emphasis on analytical thinking and real-world problem solving. You will learn how different forms of information technology operate within an organisation and how to align IT solutions with business goals, bridging technical capabilities with strategic needs. Through a balance of theory and hands-on practice, you will graduate ready to deliver innovative IT and data management solutions with confidence, while earning a dual degree award from Taylor’s University and the University of the West of England (UWE). Career pathways include roles such as system administrator, IT analyst, software developer, or information security analyst, all highly relevant in today’s fast-paced and security-conscious digital world.

curriculum.en: The programme offers a comprehensive curriculum that balances core theory with applied learning. Key areas of study include System Architecture, Software Development, Web Programming & Web Technologies, Human-Computer Interface (HCI), and; Database Management Systems – Master how to store, retrieve, and organise data for business and technical applications.; You will study computer software and systems networks to gain a clear view of how IT infrastructure supports business operations. These modules strengthen your data management skills while preparing you for high-demand roles such as system administrator, IT analyst, or developer.; Our degree programme is fully compatible with the; Taylor's Curriculum Framework; , which offers you the flexibility to mix and match study modules.; Primary Major; This component consists of Common Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Common Core; Year 1; Database Systems; Computer Architecture and Organisation; Discrete Structures; Object Oriented Programming; Data Structures and Algorithms; Operating Systems; Systems Analysis and Design; Web and Mobile Systems; Year 2; Computer Networks; System Integration and Architecture; System Paradigms; Ideating Start-up; Specialisation modules; Year 3; Capstone Project I; Professional Practices and Information Security; Capstone Project II; Human Computer Interaction; Industrial Training; *Work-based Learning mode or Technopreneurship mode available in third year. (Taught & Accessed by Academics & Industry); Students must select their specialisation during enrolment. It is advised to make changes of specialisation within Year 1. Take note that any change of specialisation during studies can impact study duration and fees.; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Specialisations (Compulsory Modules); In this Bachelor of Information Technology programme, you will have the opportunity to specialise in one of the following areas: Internet Technologies, Business Intelligence and Analytics, or Game Design. By choosing one of these specialisations, you will gain in-depth knowledge and skills in your chosen area of expertise. Our experienced faculty members, industry collaborations, and cutting-edge resources will support your learning journey and provide you with the necessary tools to excel in your specialisation.; Internet Technologies (Dual Award); If you choose the Internet Technologies specialisation, you will dive into the technical field that encompasses the skills needed to develop applications on the Internet or Internet-based systems. You will learn about e-commerce, cloud computing, mobile technologies, and web-based technologies. This specialisation equips you with the knowledge and skills to create innovative and dynamic solutions in the digital realm.; Modules; Mobile Applications Development

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: Entry Requirements Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? Our programme offers an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about the field of Applied Computing. To ensure a smooth admission process, please take note of our entry requirements listed below. Fulfilling one of the requirements listed below: A Bachelor’s degree (Level 6, MQF) in Computing or related fields with a minimum CGPA of 2.50, as accepted by the HEP Senate; OR A Bachelor’s degree (Level 6, MQF) in Computing or related fields with a minimum CGPA of 2.00 and not meeting a CGPA of 2.50 can be accepted subject to a thorough rigorous assessment as determined by the HEP; OR Other qualifications equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree (Level 6, MQF) in Computing or related fields recognisedby the Government of Malaysia must fulfil the requirement on item 1 or 2. Application via APEL A is allowed. For the requirements please refer to the index page. A Bachelor’s degree (Level 6, MQF) in Non-Computing field with a minimum CGPA of 2.00 can be accepted subject to a thorough rigorous assessment as determined by the HEP to identify the appropriate prerequisite courses that equivalent to their working experience in Computing or related fields; OR A Bachelor’s degree (Level 6, MQF) in Non-Computing field with a minimum CGPA of 2.00 can be accepted subject to appropriate prerequisite courses.

description.en: Our Master in Applied Computing programme is designed to foster innovation and nurture future technology leaders. We are committed to developing critical talent for the knowledge economy while strengthening academic-industry partnerships across disciplines. This prestigious programme prepares you to lead through specialisations in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and our newest track in Cybersecurity. Artificial Intelligence explores the complexities of machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing. Data Science delves into big data analytics, statistical modelling, and data visualisation, while Cybersecurity equips students to design, defend, and respond to evolving digital threats across systems and networks. With only a select cohort admitted each intake, you'll benefit from close mentorship by experienced faculty, going on to drive innovation at research labs and tech firms.

description.en: This programme empowers you to become a leader in innovation and technology. You'll gain the expertise to design and develop advanced computing solutions by applying the principles of software engineering to tackle complex industry and societal challenges, building scalable and secure digital systems. Delivered in English, the programme supports high-impact research in areas such as cybersecurity, data systems and big data, and ICT, all aligned with both national and global priorities. Throughout your studies, you will push boundaries in cybersecurity, data systems, or ICT, while contributing research that influences real-world practices. You will also collaborate closely with technology leaders through the University’s strong industry network, gaining direct exposure to contemporary challenges and emerging opportunities in the digital economy.

description.en: In the Master in Applied Computing (MAC) programme, we believe in equipping our students with the knowledge, skills, and mindset needed to thrive in today's rapidly evolving technological landscape. As a student in the online MAC programme at Taylor’s University, ranked World’s Top 100 for Data Science & AI (QS Subject Rankings 2025), you’ll access the same world-class curriculum as our on-campus programme. Designed for working professionals, you’ll build in-demand skills flexibly, without pausing your career. Our experienced faculty members, experts in their fields, will guide you through engaging coursework and hands-on projects that reflect real-world challenges. Note: Taylor's 100% Online Postgraduate Programmes are strictly available for students from countries which endorse Online Learning.

curriculum.en: In this programme, we prioritise the development of essential skills that will set you up for success in software-related computing fields. We understand the importance of honing your critical reasoning and technical writing abilities, as well as enhancing your professional presentation skills.; Taylor's 100% Online Postgraduate Programmes offer busy learners with multiple commitments or international learners the life-changing and career-building opportunity to pursue a Master’s or Postgraduate Certificate qualification at their own pace.; These programmes are flexible, practical, and deliver the exceptional quality of education that Taylor’s University, the No. 1 Private University in Malaysia & Southeast Asia 4 years in a row based on QS World University Rankings 2024, is known for.; Core Modules; Programming Principles Using Python; Big Data Management; Principles of Artificial Intelligence; Principles of Data Science; Research Methodology; Capstone Project I; Capstone Project II; Specialisation 1; Specialisation 2; Specialisation 3; Note:; All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Specialisation; The Master in Applied Computing online programme offers two dynamic specialisations: Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. Opting for the Artificial Intelligence specialisation allows you to delve into machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing. Alternatively, the Data Science specialisation focuses on big data analytics, statistical modelling, and data visualisation.; Data Science; Data Engineering; Data Analytics and Machine Learning; Data Visualisation; Artificial Intelligence; Image and Text Processing; Robotic Automation Using AI Techniques; Data Analytics and Machine Learning

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: Entry Requirements We offer two entry pathways for this PhD programme, which are normal mode and prior to publication mode. Our PhD by Prior Publication mode provides a unique pathway for you to achieve a Doctoral award based on your existing body of work. We recognise the value of your prior publications and include them as a significant part of your submission for the Doctoral award. Normal Mode Pre-requisites: A Master’s degree (Level 7, MQF) in the field of Computing or related fields as accepted by the HEP Senate; OR A Master’s degree (Level 7, MQF) in non-Computing fields with a minimum of FIVE (5) years of working experience in the field of computing or related fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses as determined by the HEP; OR A Master’s degree (Level 7, MQF) in non-Computing fields with less than FIVE (5) years of working experience in the field of computing or related fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses as determined by the HEP and subject to rigorous internal assessment; OR Other qualifications equivalent to a Master’s degree in the field of Computing or related fields recognised by the Government of Malaysia must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses as determined by the HEP.
programmes.officialLanguageRequirement: International Students Achieve a minimum of Band 4 in MUET or equivalent to CEFR (Mid B2). Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university. Prior Publication Mode You will need to fulfil one of the below Obtain a master's degree in the field or related fields accepted by the HEP Senate Obtain other qualifications equivalent to a master's degree recognised by the Government of Malaysia Candidates without a related qualification in the field/s or working experience in the relevant fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses determined by the HEP In addition to the above criteria, those who want to join Doctoral Degree by Retrospective or Prior Publication mode must include the below to the formal application: Minimum of 5 publications or equivalent works in alignment with the theme of the specialisation; An executive summary of the above publications to demonstrate the applicant’s contribution to knowledge in the field; A list of scholarly published work; For international candidates, evidence of English Language Proficiency as determined by the intake standards approved by the Senate A Selection Committee must be established to review the formal application for PhD by Retrospective or Prior Publication and recommend to the Senate to obtain approval. Criteria for published works Published work must encompass high-quality journals, monographs, books, research-based chapters in books, electronic publications which have not been used to obtain other awards or deemed a part of those awards. The publications must be published within a period not exceeding ten (10) years from the date of submission. For the five (5) nominated publications, the candidate must be the principal author with the contributions of others clearly defined. Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.

description.en: Our Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Computer Science programme is designed to support and challenge graduate students who are passionate about computing to develop a deep understanding of algorithmic foundations and engage in rigorous scientific research. This PhD programme builds a strong foundation in core computer science principles, while enabling exploration of advanced topics such as algorithms, data structures, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and more. Through this, you’ll gain the expertise to address complex challenges and drive meaningful innovation in a rapidly evolving field. With strong academic mentorship and a research-focused environment, the programme is well-regarded among aspiring scholars and computing professionals. As a PhD student, you’ll have the opportunity to conduct original research and sharpen your expertise in computer science or information technology, preparing you to deliver impactful solutions across academia, industry, or applied research.

description.en: Throughout this highly sought-after programme, you will learn how to create engaging environments that incorporate elements of physical, augmented reality, virtual reality, and interactive technologies. By leveraging these cutting-edge tools, you will be able to gain the skills that make graduates leaders in this emerging field.

curriculum.en: Our curriculum is designed to nurture your creativity and enhance your digital proficiency. You will develop interdisciplinary skills and processes that are essential for the future of spatial design. Our experienced faculty members, who are industry practitioners themselves, will guide you through hands-on projects and provide insights into the latest trends and advancements in the field.; Programme Core; This component consists of Primary Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Year 1; Spatial Design I; Spatial Design II; Environment Design; 3D Modelling; Application Design I; Application Design II; Games Studies; Programming; Embedded Systems; Lighting Interactive Design; Year 2; Specialisation modules; Year 3; Choose ONE(1) of the pathway option:; Conventional; • Multidisciplinary Project I; • Multidisciplinary Project II; Technopreneurship; • Technopreneurship Project I; • Technopreneurship Project II; Work-based Learning; • Industry Project I (WBL); • Industry Project II (WBL); Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Specialisations; You will need to choose one of the options below:; Option 1: Smart Homes Design; Home Automation; Advanced Modelling & Animation; Advanced Home Automation; Internet of Things (IoT); Computer Vision and Natural Language Processing; Experiential Design; Games Development; Option 2: Smart Environment Design

evidence.sourceText: Bachelor of Interactive Spatial Design (Honours)
3-year
February, April, September

Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? Our programme offers an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about the field of Interactive Spatial Design. To ensure a smooth admission process, please take note of our entry requirements listed below. Prerequisites SPM/O-Level with Pre-University/Foundation Pass SPM/O-level or equivalent with 5 credits for entry with Pre-U/Foundation qualification (Except for UEC). SPM/O-Level with Diploma Pass SPM/O-level or equivalent with 3 credits for entry with Diploma qualification. Visual Test Pass Visual Test (Taylor’s FID, DID and FNBE are exempted from the Entrance Test) Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university. Entry Pathway AUSMAT (SACEi) ATAR 55 A Level Min. grades CDD Canadian Pre-University (CPU) Average of 55% in 6 subjects Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) CC Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) A Pass with UEC with Min. 5 Bs Taylor's Foundation / Diploma Pass FNBE with min. CGPA 2.00 Pass FID with min. CGPA 2.00 Pass Taylor's Diploma with min. CGPA 2.00 Other Taylor's Foundation with min CGPA 2.

English Requirements LOCAL STUDENTS MUET/IELTS/TOEFL/UEC English Pass English Taylor’s EET Overall Score 4.0 Taylor’s IEN Level 2- Grade C Pre-University/Diploma Completed Pre-U/Diploma that was conducted in English INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS Achieve a minimum score of Band 3 in MUET or equivalent to CEFR Low B2. Completed Pre-U/Diploma that was conducted in English Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.

MYR 115,790 (Local) USD 34,282 (International) We offer the overseas transfer options of completing your design programme at one of our established partner universities. To support your journey, you can also explore the scholarships offered here .

Effective 1 July 2025, a 6% Service Tax will be imposed on non-Malaysian citizens, applicable to all fees and charges, except International Security Deposit and EMGS application fees. Fees shown in the Fee Schedule are exclusive of the 6% Service Tax. The Service Tax rate and taxable fee components are subject to change as determined by government regulations.

To ensure a smooth admission process, please take note of our entry requirements listed below. Prerequisites SPM/O-Level with Pre-Univesity/Foundation Pass SPM/O-level or equivalent with 5 credits with foundation qualification (Except for UEC). SPM/O-Level with Diploma Pass SPM/O-level or equivalent with 3 credits for entry with Diploma qualification. Visual Test Pass Visual Test (Taylor'’s FID, DID and FNBE are exempted from the Entrance Test) Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university. Entry Pathway AUSMAT (SACEi) Min. ATAR 60 A Level Min. grades DD Canadian Pre-University (CPU) Min. average of 55% in 6 subjects Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) CC Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) Pass with min. 5Bs Taylor’s Foundation in Design (FID) Pass with min. CGPA 2.00 Taylor’s Foundation in Natural and Built Environments (FNBE) Pass with min. CGPA 2.00 Other Taylor's Foundation Pass with min. CGPA 2.00 Taylor’s Diploma in Interior Design (DID) Pass with min. CGPA 2.00 International Baccalaureate (IB) Min 24 points in 6 subjects Monash University Foundation Year (MUFY) Overall 50% Other Qualifications Foundation from institution recognised by Malaysian Government with min. CGPA 2.00 Diploma from institution recognised by Malaysian Government with min. CGPA 2.00 MoE Matriculation with min. CGPA 2.00 A pass in DKM/DKLM/DVM in suitable fields with a min. CGPA of 2.50 subject to Senate approval (Note: The HEPs are to conduct screening and provide necessary guidance specific to the discipline of the programme); OR A pass in DKM / DLKM / DVM with a min. CGPA of 2.00 and at least have two (2) years working experience in a related discipline. The institution need to conduct a bridging program in the duration of the student following the programme to support the existing curriculum. The duration of the bridging program shall not exceed one (1) year or two (2) Semesters of study. Any other qualification recognised by Malaysian govt. Application via APEL A is allowed. Notes : All information is subject to change. The above entry requirements serve as a guideline. Readers are responsible to verify the information by contacting the university's Admissions Department.

curriculum.en: Through problem-based and studio-based approaches, you'll delve into the fundamental processes of design theory and practice. Experience the design thinking process firsthand, enabling you to analyse, evaluate, and propose innovative and creative design solutions. Our prescribed modules will equip you with the necessary skill sets to conceptualise and create aesthetically appealing outputs that are not only creative and functional but also entertaining, engaging, and communicable.; Prepare for captivating careers in fashion retail, digital clothing creation, and more. Our programme is compatible with the Taylor's Curriculum Framework, allowing you to mix and match study modules to tailor your learning experience.; Programme Core; This component consists of Primary Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Year 1; Design Principles; Introduction to Fashion Design; Introduction to Pattern Drafting and Garment Making; Fashion Project I; Garment Draping; Fashion Illustration; Fashion History; Intercultural Design; Year 2; Fashion Project II; Introduction to Pattern Technology; Ethical and Sustainable Fashion; Innovative Industry Project; Innovative Pattern Drafting Project; Fashion Entrepreneurship; Digital Illustration; Free Electives 1; Free Electives 2; Free Electives 3; *Note:; Industry Training module is offered in Year 2; Student able to opt for 1 semester abroad/mobility programme in Year 2 (Semester 4); Year 3; Fashion Design Technology Final Project I; Garment Creation Technology I; Fashion Communication and Visual Merchandising; Fashion Design Technology Final Project II; Garment Creation Technology II; International Fashion; Free Electives 4; Free Electives 5; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; University Core; This component aims to develop critical thinking, build up social intelligence and cultivate civic responsibility as well as broaden cultural knowledge. These consist of compulsory and nationally mandated study modules required by the Malaysian Ministry of Higher Education.

With our comprehensive specialisations, graduates are highly sought after by major studios, agencies, and tech giants: a testament to our industry-aligned curriculum.

curriculum.en: Our curriculum is carefully designed to ensure that you gain a comprehensive understanding of design principles and methodologies. You will learn to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to tackle design challenges, while also honing your creativity and artistic abilities.; We believe in a holistic approach to design education, which is why our programme is designed to be compatible with the new; Taylor's Curriculum Framework; . This framework allows you to personalise your learning experience by mixing and matching study modules that align with your interests and career goals.; Primary Major; This component consists of Common Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Common Core; Year 1; Typography; Illustration and Visual Narrative; Digital Photography and Imaging; Design Research Methodology; Video and Sound Production; Interactive Design; Advanced Typography; Intercultural Design; Design Principles; Year 2; Design Research Dissertation; Minor Project; Major Project I; Specialisation Modules (Refer to specialisation options); Year 3; Extension 1 / Free Elective 1 / Minor 1; Industry Training; Major Project II; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Specialisation; In our Bachelor of Design in Creative Media programme, we offer a range of specialisations to cater to your specific interests and career goals.; Graphic Design; The Graphic Design specialisation encompasses a dynamic process that combines implicit and explicit knowledge, as well as intuitive and reasoned thinking. It integrates art, technology, user, organisational, and practice-based knowledge and skills within both individual and team contexts. This specialisation fosters the development of these attributes in students, enhancing learning, employability, and future growth. Join us to cultivate your creativity and expertise in Graphic Design.; Design Research Dissertation; Minor Project; Brand Corporate Identity; Packaging and Merchandising Design; Publishing Design; Creative Brand Strategy; Digital and Social Media Communication; Advanced Interactive Design

Our programme offers an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about the field of Master of Computer Science. To ensure a smooth admission process, please take note of our entry requirements listed below. Fulfilling one of the requirements listed below: Bachelor's Degree (Tier 1) A Bachelor's degree (Level 6, MQF) or equivalent with minimum CGPA of 2.75 in the relevant field, as accepted by the HEP's Senate; Candidates with a Bachelor's degree (Level 6, MQF) or equivalent with at least CGPA of 2.50 in the relevant field and has not achieved CGPA 2.75, can be accepted subject to rigorous internal assessment; Candidates with a Bachelor’s degree (Level 6, MQF) or equivalent with CGPA of less than 2.50 in the relevant field and a minimum of five (5) years working experience in the relevant field; Other relevant equivalent qualifications recognized by the Malaysian Government. AND Pass an interview OR submission of a portfolio determined by the HEP as required.

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: We offered two entry pathway for this PhD programme, which is normal mode and prior to publication mode. Our PhD by Prior Publication mode provides a unique pathway for you to achieve a Doctoral award based on your existing body of work. We recognize the value of your prior publications and include them as a significant part of your submission for the Doctoral award. Normal Mode Pre-requisites: A Recognised Master's Degree preferably in Art and Design or a relevant field Equivalent qualification and / or experience which is recognised by the Senate / institution Candidates are required to submit a research proposal; and A Pass in an interview.
programmes.officialLanguageRequirement: International Students Required to achieve a minimum Malaysian University English Test (MUET) with Band 4 OR its equivalent score of 6.5 in IELTS. (May join IEN preparatory course and achieve the IELTS score) The validity of the IELTS or equivalent is within 2 years from the date of the examination.\ *Students without a qualification in the related field but with relevant working experience requires to fulfil the following conditions: a) CGPA above 2.50 must have at least one (1) year of relevant working experience; or b) CGPA 2.00 to 2.50 must have at least five (5) years of relevant working experience; In addition, students will need to undergo a rigorous internal assessment Bachelor to PhD Track A Bachelor's degree with the following conditions: A Bachelor's degree in the field or related fields with first-class (CGPA of 3.67 or higher) or its equivalent from academic or Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme; Undergo internal assessment; AND Any other requirement of the HEP Note : Bachelor's degree candidates who are registered for master's degree programmes may apply to convert to the doctoral degree programmes subjected to the following conditions: Within 1 year for full time and within 2 years for part-time candidates; Having shown competency and capability in conducting research at doctoral level through rigorous internal evaluation, and approval of the Taylor's University Senate. Students without a qualification in the related fields or relevant working experience requires to undergo and pass a bridging module. Any of the condition of the above would require student’s research proposal to be approved. All information is subject to change. The above entry requirements serve as a guideline. Readers are responsible to verify the information by contacting the university’s Admissions Department. Prior Publication Mode You will need to fulfil one of the below Obtain a master's degree in the field or related fields accepted by the HEP Senate Obtain other qualifications equivalent to a master's degree recognised by the Government of Malaysia Candidates without a related qualification in the field/s or working experience in the relevant fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses determined by the HEP In addition to the above criteria, those who want to join Doctoral Degree by Retrospective or Prior Publication mode must include the below to the formal application: Minimum of 5 publications or equivalent works in alignment with the theme of the specialisation; An executive summary of the above publications to demonstrate the applicant’s contribution to knowledge in the field; A list of scholarly published work; For international candidates, evidence of English Language Proficiency as determined by the intake standards approved by the Senate A Selection Committee must be established to review the formal application for PhD by Retrospective or Prior Publication and recommend to the Senate to obtain approval. Criteria for published works Published work must encompass high-quality journals, monographs, books, research-based chapters in books, electronic publications which have not been used to obtain other awards or deemed a part of those awards. The publications must be published within a period not exceeding ten (10) years from the date of submission. For the five (5) nominated publications, the candidate must be the principal author with the contributions of others clearly defined. Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.

Our flexible curriculum allows you to tailor your studies, selecting modules and electives that resonate with your research focus. You will be guided by experienced faculty members who are experts in their respective fields, providing mentorship and support as you navigate your research journey.; Key Research Areas; At Taylor's University, we believe research can help shape the future. curriculum.en: This degree programme is compatible with; Taylor's Curriculum Framework; that allows students to mix & match study modules.; Primary Core; This component consists of core subjects, which are primary modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Year 1; Philosophy and Curriculum Design; Education, School and Society; Teaching and Managing Diverse Learners in the Classroom; Learning, Assessment and Feedback; Year 2; Professional Practice 1 (PP1); Professional Practice 2 (PP2); Year 3; New Pedagogies – Digital Tools and Resources; The Reflective Practitioner: Teachers Investigate Their Work; Action Research Project; Theory into Practice; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Specialisation; This component consists of specialisation subjects, which are primary modules based on the chosen specialisation that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Specialisation: Primary Education; Year 1; Teaching Language Arts; Teaching Primary School English Language; Language Use and Society; Number & Algebra; Year 2; Measurement & Geometry; Statistics; Science - Systems and Cycles; Science - Energy and Interactions; Year 3; Nature of Science; Specialisation: Teaching of English; Year 1; Academic Reading & Writing; ELT Methodology; Introduction to Applied Linguistics I

fee.note: Note: Fees will be reviewed annually. For the avoidance of doubt, Taylor’s reserves the right to revise the fee payable for any given semester. Effective 1 July 2025, a 6% Service Tax will be imposed on non-Malaysian citizens, applicable to all fees and charges, except International Security Deposit and EMGS application fees. Fees shown in the Fee Schedule are exclusive of the 6% Service Tax. The Service Tax rate and taxable fee components are subject to change as determined by government regulations.

description.en: You'll gain a deep understanding of topics such as educational psychology, instructional strategies, assessment and evaluation, and classroom management. The strong foundation in pedagogical knowledge empowers you to design and deliver effective and engaging lessons, establishing you as a preferred candidate for schools across Asia. Due to the programme's unique structure and demand, limited seats are available each intake, ensuring personalised guidance throughout your journey.

description.en: As part of this immersive programme, you will engage deeply with education research and examine current developments in policy and administration. You will learn to critically analyse and evaluate educational frameworks across diverse settings, refining your professional expertise while shaping a rigorous and reflective learning experience aligned with your specialised interests. With limited places each intake, you benefit from personalised guidance, strong research support, and opportunities to create lasting impact within the education sector.

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: We offer two entry pathways for this PhD programme, normal mode and prior to publication mode. Our PhD by Prior Publication mode provides a unique pathway for you to achieve a Doctoral award based on your existing body of work. We recognise the value of your prior publications and include them as a significant part of your submission for the Doctoral award. Normal Mode Pre-Requisites A Master’s degree in Education field (Level 7, MQF) as accepted by the HEP Senate; or A Master’s degree in non-education must undergo prerequisite courses; or Other relevant equivalent qualifications recognised by Malaysian government as equivalent to the above requirements; or A Bachelor’s degree with the following conditions: or A Bachelor's degree in the field or related fields with first-class (CGPA of 3.67 or higher) or its equivalent from an academic or Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme; Undergo internal assessment; and Approval of the HEP Senate A Bachelor’s degree candidates who are registered for Master’s degree programmes may apply to convert to the Doctoral degree programmes subjected to the following conditions: Within 1 year for full time and within 2 years for part-time candidates; Having shown competency and capability in conducting research at doctoral level through rigorous internal evaluation by the HEP; and Approval of the HEP Senate For International Student
programmes.officialLanguageRequirement: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 79 (Internet Based Test) (May join IEN preparatory course and achieve the IELTS score) The validity of the IELTS or equivalent is within 2 years from the date of the examination. Accelerated PhD Bachelor's degree candidates who are registered for master's degree programmes may apply to convert to the doctoral degree programmes subjected to the following conditions Within 1 year for full time and within 2 years for part-time candidates; Having shown competency and capability in conducting research at doctoral level through rigorous internal evaluation. Approval of the Taylor's University Senate. Note: Any of the condition of the above would require student's research proposal to be approved. All information is subject to change. The above entry requirements serve as a guideline. Readers are responsible to verify the information by contacting the university’s Admissions Department. Prior Publication Mode You will need to fulfil one of the below: Obtain a master's degree in the field or related fields accepted by the HEP Senate Obtain other qualifications equivalent to a master's degree recognised by the Government of Malaysia Candidates without a related qualification in the field/s or working experience in the relevant fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses determined by the HEP In addition to the above criteria, those who want to join Doctoral Degree by Retrospective or Prior Publication mode must include the below to the formal application: Minimum of 5 publications or equivalent works in alignment with the theme of the specialisation; An executive summary of the above publications to demonstrate the applicant’s contribution to knowledge in the field; A list of scholarly published work; The minimum language proficiency of the candidates must be determined by the HEP consistent with applicable programme standards or based on the needs of the programme, i.e., learning outcomes and the medium of instruction. A Selection Committee must be established to review the formal application for PhD by Retrospective or Prior Publication and recommend to the Senate to obtain approval. Criteria for published works Published work must encompass high-quality journals, monographs, books, research-based chapters in books, electronic publications which have not been used to obtain other awards or deemed a part of those awards. The publications or productions must be published or produced within a period not exceeding ten (10) years from the date of submission. For the five (5) nominated publications or productions, the candidate must be the principal author or creator with the contributions of others clearly defined. description.en: As a doctoral student at Taylor's, you'll engage in advanced research, critical analysis, and scholarly inquiry in your chosen field. With a focus on academic rigour and personalised mentorship, our programme welcomes a select group of scholars each intake. Faculty members, renowned experts in various educational areas, will provide valuable insights and support your research, in a collaborative environment where your ideas can flourish.

A Selection Committee must be established to review the formal application for PhD by Retrospective or Prior Publication and recommend to the Senate to obtain approval. Criteria for published works Published work must encompass high-quality journals, monographs, books, research-based chapters in books, electronic publications which have not been used to obtain other awards or deemed a part of those awards. The publications or productions must be published or produced within a period not exceeding ten (10) years from the date of submission. For the five (5) nominated publications or productions, the candidate must be the principal author or creator with the contributions of others clearly defined. description.en: Our reputation for producing innovative and environmentally conscious engineers has made our programme a highly sought-after choice for solution-oriented individuals, resulting in a competitive applicant pool. This reflects the ambition of students who are driven to create sustainable solutions for a better future. Throughout the programme, you will delve into the core principles of chemical engineering, developing a sound understanding of the theories and concepts that underpin the field. From thermodynamics to fluid mechanics, you will explore various topics essential to chemical engineering and craft solutions that sustain both business success and planetary health.

curriculum.en: Throughout the programme, you will delve into the intricacies of electrical and electronic engineering. You will gain a comprehensive understanding of key concepts, theories, and principles that form the backbone of the discipline. From circuit analysis to power systems, electronic devices to signal processing, you will explore a wide range of topics essential to electrical and electronic engineering.; You will have the opportunity to work on sophisticated scientific and industrial technology projects, gaining first-hand experience in creating, designing, and implementing electrical and electronic systems.; Primary Major; This component consists of Common Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Common Core; Year 1; Engineering Mathematics and Modelling I; Engineering Design and Analysis; Circuits and Signals; Programming Techniques; Electromagnetic Fields & Waves; Engineering Mathematics and Modelling II; Digital and Analogue Electronics; Year 2; Communication Systems; Microprocessors and Computer Architecture; Engineering Design and Project Management; Electrical Power and Machines; Flexible Studies (Choose Minor OR Free Electives package); Year 3; Power System Analysis and Protection; Power Electronics and Industrial Drives; Automatic Control and Instrumentation; High Voltage Engineering; Industrial Training; Year 4; Electrical & Electronic Engineering Group Project I; Final Year Engineering Project I; Electrical Energy Generation and Utilisation; Electrical & Electronic Engineering Group Project II; Final Year Engineering Project II; Professional Engineers and Society; Note: All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Specialisation; Specialisation 1: Renewable Energy; Sustainable Buildings; Engineering Economics and Environmental Impact; Renewable and Alternative Energies; Energy Storage and Transmission; Specialisation 2: AI for Engineers

curriculum.en: Throughout the programme, you will gain a deep understanding of the principles and technologies that drive these industries forward. You will explore the intricate workings of automotive systems, power generation processes, aerospace engineering, and advanced manufacturing techniques. By immersing yourself in these subjects, you will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to excel in a rapidly evolving technological landscape.; In addition to industry-specific knowledge, we prioritise the development of your physics and mathematical skills. These foundational skills are crucial in the digital economy, enabling you to analyse complex problems, make data-driven decisions, and contribute to innovative solutions. By honing your abilities in these areas, you will be well-prepared for a wide range of careers that can positively impact the lives of many.; Primary Major; This component consists of Common Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Common Core; Year 1; Engineering Mathematics and Modelling I; Engineering Mathematics and Modelling II; Engineering Design and Analysis; Programming Techniques; Materials and Manufacturing; Thermofluid Engineering I; Introduction to Electronics & Electrical Power Machines; Year 2; Engineering Design and Project Management; Thermofluid Engineering II; Engineering Solid Mechanics; Year 3; Electronics & Microprocessors; Automatic Control and Instrumentation; Engineering Dynamics; Finite Element Method and Simulation; Mechanical Vibration; Specialisation Module; Industrial Training; Year 4; Final Year Engineering Project I; Final Year Engineering Project II; Mechanical Engineering Group Project I; Mechanical Engineering Group Project II; Professional Engineers and Society; Note: All information is subject to change. description.en: Throughout this programme, you will explore the design, development, and control of smart systems and devices that combine mechanical, electronic, and software components. The curriculum is carefully crafted to cover a wide range of topics, including robotics, automation, sensors and actuators, embedded systems, and control engineering. You will learn how to design and implement intelligent systems, working with cutting-edge technologies that shape the future of industries such as manufacturing, automotive, healthcare, and aerospace. One of the key features of our programme is the emphasis on hands-on learning and industry engagement. You will have the opportunity to participate in practical projects, internships, and collaborative research, allowing you to apply your theoretical knowledge to real-world challenges. This approach ensures that you graduate with the technical expertise and problem-solving skills required to excel in the evolving field of mechatronics. As we welcome applicants from all over the world, we are thrilled to see many students recognising the exceptional quality and opportunities our programme offers, and their drive to be selected in a competitive admissions process.

description.en: Through advanced study, you will build critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and problem-solving capabilities that are essential in today’s complex engineering landscape. With a strong emphasis on research and applied practice, you will learn to address real-world engineering challenges and develop innovative solutions that contribute meaningfully to society, industry, and academia.

curriculum.en: Our MSc in Engineering attracts highly motivated individuals from diverse backgrounds who are drawn by the programme’s strong reputation for academic excellence, innovation, and practical impact. Successful applicants gain the opportunity to work alongside experienced faculty, industry experts, and active research communities — making the programme both intellectually stimulating and deeply rewarding.; Through a thoughtfully designed curriculum, you will develop advanced competencies in project management, collaborative research, and technical communication. These skills prepare you not only to excel in your chosen area of specialisation but also to embrace lifelong learning and adapt to the rapid technological transformations shaping the future of engineering.; The Master of Science in Engineering blends advanced theoretical knowledge with hands-on application, allowing you to tailor your studies to align with your professional interests and career ambitions.; Programme Highlights:; Theoretical Knowledge:; Deepen your understanding of advanced engineering concepts and research methodologies.; Laboratory Work:; Apply theoretical insights through hands-on experiments in industry-standard facilities.; Independent Research:; Conduct a thesis project under the guidance of expert academic supervisors.; Industry Placements:; Gain real-world exposure through collaborations, internships, and applied projects.; By integrating rigorous research with experiential learning, the programme challenges you to push boundaries, explore innovative solutions, and make meaningful contributions to solving real-world engineering challenges — equipping you for leadership roles in academia, industry, and beyond.; Research Methodology; Students are required to pass the following modules (6 credit hours) in the first year of their candidature:; Year 1; Research Method for Social Science (Core Module); Qualitative Research Methods / Quantitative Research Methods; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Key Research Areas; At Taylor's University, we believe research can help shape the future. Our postgraduate research programmes cover a broad range of topics with the aim to help shape the future in the aspects of society, technology, economy, and environment.; Click here to learn more about our; research area; .; Hiring Graduate Student; More than 300 postgraduates have chosen Taylor's to fulfil their research aspiration. Join us and contribute to our innovative and progressive research projects; here; .

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: Entry Requirements We offered two entry pathway for this PhD programme, which is normal mode and prior to publication mode. Our PhD by Prior Publication mode provides a unique pathway for you to achieve a Doctoral award based on your existing body of work. We recognise the value of your prior publications and include them as a significant part of your submission for the Doctoral award. Normal Mode Pre-requisites: Masters in the Engineering/Engineering Technology or its equivalent; OR Passed Bachelor's degree Engineering/Engineering Technology or its equivalent with min. CGPA 3.67 and registered as a Masters candidate and passed related qualifying assessment; OR Any other equivalent qualification recognized by Malaysian government OR accepted by the Taylor's University Senate and Any of the above condition would require student's research proposal to be approved.

Approval of the Taylor's University Senate. If Your Bachelor Degree Are From Different Fields Students without a qualification in the related fields or relevant working experience requires to undergo and pass a bridging module. description.en: Our Doctor of Philosophy in Engineering programme is designed to provide students with an expanded mental capacity, enabling them to engage in advanced research within their chosen field and contribute to the generation of new knowledge. We aim to cultivate independent researchers who can push the boundaries of knowledge in a global context. We are delighted by the strong applications we receive from aspiring students, who recognise the value of our programme and are eager to earn a place in their preferred intake. Throughout the programme, you will develop the necessary skills and expertise to conduct thorough and independent research. By engaging in cutting-edge research projects, you will have the opportunity to make significant contributions to your field of study. Our faculty, renowned for their expertise and research accomplishments, will guide and mentor you as you navigate the research process. We recommend that you register your interest for a spot early to have a higher chance of securing your place.

description.en: You will learn essential areas such as hospitality operations, marketing, human resource management, and service innovation, supported by practical training in industry-standard facilities. With strong industry links and international exposure, you will graduate with the confidence to take on leadership roles in hospitality and across industries. Beyond management skills, this degree expands your job opportunities in event planning, travel services, and luxury brand management. You will also develop adaptability, creativity, and problem-solving abilities, qualities that ensure you can thrive in diverse hospitality settings, both locally and internationally.

curriculum.en: Throughout the 12-month programme, you will delve into various interdisciplinary subjects that encompass the diverse aspects of hospitality management. You will explore topics such as strategic management, marketing, finance, operations, human resources, and entrepreneurship, all within the context of the hospitality industry.; One of the key strengths of the programme is its industry orientation. You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced industry professionals, participate in industry visits and internships, and engage in real-world projects that simulate the challenges and complexities of the hospitality industry. This hands-on approach ensures that you develop practical skills that are highly valued by employers and enables you to apply your knowledge in real-world settings.; Primary Core; This component consists of core subjects, which are primary modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Year 1; Principles of Marketing; Business of Hospitality, Food and Leisure Management; Events and Entertainment; Design for Events; Social Media for Events; Trends and Issues in International Event Management; Conventions and Meetings Management; Event Sponsorship and Funding; Events Project Management; Year 2; Research Methods; French Basic; Events Operations; Sustainable Event Management; Event Technology; Exhibition Management; Year 3; Research Project; Live Event Project; Event and Tourism Risk Management; Internship; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; University Core; This component aims to develop critical thinking, build up social intelligence and cultivate civic responsibility as well as broaden cultural knowledge. These consist of compulsory and nationally-mandated study modules required by the Malaysian Ministry of Higher Education.; Penghayatan Etika dan Peradaban / Bahasa Melayu Komunikasi 2; Falsafah dan Isu Semasa; Emotional Intelligence in Action (EI); Kursus Integriti Dan Antirasuah (KIAR); Social Innovation Project; Note; :; Students are requested to take Bahasa Kebangsaan A if they do not obtain a Credit for Bahasa Malaysia in SPM.; All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; Flexible Education

description.en: Through this programme, you will gain the knowledge and practical skills needed to contribute meaningfully to the growth and transformation of the tourism sector. You will also develop forward-thinking capabilities in planning and decision-making, enabling you to respond effectively to global trends and challenges in tourism and hospitality. As this highly sought-after programme offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of travel and the broader hospitality industry, early application is encouraged to secure your spot in our competitive intake.

curriculum.en: As a full-scale bachelor of tourism curriculum, this programme covers topics such as tourism marketing, destination management, sustainable development, event management, and cultural studies—ensuring a 360° understanding of travel services and sectors. Students will be equipped with functional and managerial skills, as well as knowledge in business, communication, culture and arts, events, and tourism studies. The curriculum has been strengthened with international and local content, preparing graduates to work in different parts of the world.; The programme is highly recognised by the industry and was awarded the Business Events (BE) Education Excellence Award and accredited as an International Centre of Excellence in Event Management.; This degree is compatible with the new Taylor's Curriculum Framework that allows students to mix & match study modules.; Primary Major; This component consists of core subjects, which are primary modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Year 1; Principles of Marketing; Business of Hospitality, Food and Leisure Management; Leisure Attraction Management; Destination Geography and Analysis; Strategic Destination Marketing and Branding; Tourism Economics; Tourism Business Management; Understanding Entrepreneurialism; Airline and Airport Management; Year 2; Research Methods; French Basic; Sociology of Tourism; Data and Media Analysis for Tourism; Sustainable Tourism Development; Tourism Product Design and Development; Year 3; Research Project; Tourism Integrated Project; Event and Tourism Risk Management; Internship; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; University Core; This component aims to develop critical thinking, build up social intelligence and cultivate civic responsibility as well as broaden cultural knowledge. These consist of compulsory and nationally-mandated study modules required by the Malaysian Ministry of Higher Education.; Penghayatan Etika dan Peradaban / Bahasa Melayu Komunikasi 2; Falsafah dan Isu Semasa; Emotional Intelligence in Action (EI); Kursus Integriti Dan Antirasuah (KIAR); Social Innovation Project; Note; :; Students are requested to take Bahasa Kebangsaan A if they do not obtain a Credit for Bahasa Malaysia in SPM.; All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.

programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: This programme is for individuals seeking a versatile postgraduate qualification from a QS-ranked World Top 20 university for Hospitality & Leisure Management, which unlocks opportunities in various disciplines from hotel, events and catering management to business development, entrepreneurship, marketing & PR, finance, digital transformation and more. Fulfilling one of the requirements listed below: Bachelor's Degree (Tier 1) A Bachelor's degree in the field or related fields with a CGPA ≥ 2.50, recognised by the Malaysian Government; OR Bachelor's Degree (Tier 2) Bachelor's degree in the field or related fields with a 2.00 ≤ CGPA < 2.50, recognized by the Malaysian or National Government, AND a minimum of 5 years related working experience; OR Postgraduate Diploma Postgraduate Diploma Level 7 in same field recognised by Malaysian Government; OR Other equivalent qualification Any other equivalent qualification recognised by the Malaysian Government Application via APEL A is allowed. *Students without a qualification in the related field but with relevant working experience requires to fulfil the following conditions: a) CGPA above 2.50 must have at least one (1) year of relevant working experience; or b) CGPA 2.00 to 2.50 must have at least five (5) years of relevant working experience; In addition, students will need to undergo a rigorous internal assessment

description.en: With the unique opportunity to lead in the global hospitality sector in our sought-after programme, early application is crucial to secure your place in this transformative experience. As a student of our online programme, you will benefit from a flexible and convenient learning format that allows you to study at your own pace and from anywhere in the world. Whether you are a working professional looking to advance your career or an aspiring entrepreneur eager to make your mark in the industry, this programme offers the flexibility you need to achieve your goals. Note: Taylor's 100% Online Postgraduate Programmes are strictly available for students from countries which endorse Online Learning.

description.en: This academically rigorous programme combines the best of academic knowledge and industry relevance, providing you with a comprehensive understanding of the intricacies of hospitality management. With a strong focus on practical skills and industry orientation, the programme equips you with the sophisticated tools and cutting-edge techniques necessary to excel in management careers within the hospitality sector.

curriculum.en: Throughout the 12-month programme, you will delve into various inter-disciplinary subjects that encompass the diverse aspects of hospitality management. You will explore topics such as strategic management, marketing, finance, operations, human resources, and entrepreneurship, all within the context of the hospitality industry.; One of the key strengths of the programme is its industry orientation. You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced industry professionals, participate in industry visits and internships, and engage in real-world projects that simulate the challenges and complexities of the hospitality industry. This hands-on approach ensures that you develop practical skills that are highly valued by employers and enables you to apply your knowledge in real-world settings.; Primary Modules; Year 1; Block 1; Sustainable Development in Hospitality and Tourism; Strategic Decision Making in the Hospitality Industry; Block 2; Hospitality Asset Management and Financial Planning; Disciplinary Core (Choose one from the below):; The Economics of Hospitality and Tourism; Hotel Brand Management; Block 3; Strategic Marketing; Hospitality Project Management; Block 4; Research Methodology; Quality Management; Block 5; Hospitality Application Simulation Management; Disciplinary Core (Choose either Option A or Option B); Year 2; Block 6 & 7; Dissertation Project; Internship; Disciplinary Core Option; List of Optional Discipline Core; [Choose either only one discipline core with 4 credits from Option A* (or) two discipline core with 2 credits each from Option B** based on the list provided in each block]; *Disciplinary Core Option A (block 2 & 5); The Economics of Hospitality and Tourism; Hotel Brand Management; **Disciplinary Core Option B (block 2 & 5); Hotel Industry Analytics; Innovative Hospitality Technologies; Dr Anshul Garg, Programme Director; Elevate your career in hospitality management through a blend of cutting-edge academics and real-world industry experiences. Our programme is dedicated to cultivating future leaders equipped with the skills and knowledge to thrive in the global hospitality landscape.; VIEW ALL LECTURERS; Dr Anshul Garg, Programme Director; Elevate your career in hospitality management through a blend of cutting-edge academics and real-world industry experiences. Our programme is dedicated to cultivating future leaders equipped with the skills and knowledge to thrive in the global hospitality landscape.; VIEW ALL LECTURERS

description.en: This is a programme for curious, committed minds. Students come with different goals, some aiming to teach or pursue doctoral research, others seeking to become specialists who influence industry practice or policy. What they share is a desire to ask better questions about tourism, understand its complexities, and produce work that stands up to academic and professional scrutiny. Throughout the programme, you will engage with tourism from multiple perspectives, combining theoretical grounding with practical relevance. You will explore how tourism operates across social, economic, cultural, and environmental contexts, while also examining current trends and emerging challenges shaping the field. Coursework builds a strong conceptual foundation, while the research component allows you to investigate a topic that matters to you in depth, developing analytical, critical, and research skills that are transferable well beyond graduation. By the end of the programme, you will not only understand tourism more deeply, but also be equipped to contribute new knowledge, challenge assumptions, and participate thoughtfully in shaping how tourism evolves in an increasingly complex world.

Our PhD by Prior Publication mode provides a unique pathway for you to achieve a Doctoral award based on your existing body of work. We recognise the value of your prior publications and include them as a significant part of your submission for the Doctoral award. Normal Mode Masters Masters in the field or related fields; OR Bachelor’s Degree Passed Bachelor’s degree in the field or related fields with min. CGPA 3.67 and registered as a Masters candidate and passed related qualifying assessment Other equivalent qualification Any other equivalent qualification recognized by Malaysian government or accepted by the Taylor's University Senate and Any of condition of the above would require student's research proposal to be approved.

Prior Publication Mode You will need to fulfil one of the below: Obtain a master's degree in the field or related fields accepted by the HEP Senate Obtain other qualifications equivalent to a master's degree recognised by the Government of Malaysia Candidates without a related qualification in the field/s or working experience in the relevant fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses determined by the HEP In addition to the above criteria, those who want to join Doctoral Degree by Retrospective or Prior Publication mode must include the below to the formal application: Minimum of 5 publications or equivalent works in alignment with the theme of the specialisation; An executive summary of the above publications to demonstrate the applicant’s contribution to knowledge in the field; A list of scholarly published work; The minimum language proficiency of the candidates must be determined by the HEP consistent with applicable programme standards or based on the needs of the programme, i.e., learning outcomes and the medium of instruction. A Selection Committee must be established to review the formal application for PhD by Retrospective or Prior Publication and recommend to the Senate to obtain approval. Criteria for published works Published work must encompass high-quality journals, monographs, books, research-based chapters in books, electronic publications which have not been used to obtain other awards or deemed a part of those awards. The publications or productions must be published or produced within a period not exceeding ten (10) years from the date of submission. For the five (5) nominated publications or productions, the candidate must be the principal author or creator with the contributions of others clearly defined. Notes All information is subject to change. The above entry requirements serve as a guideline. Readers are responsible to verify the information by contacting the university's Admissions Department. description.en: As a PhD candidate, you will have the opportunity to delve deep into your area of interest, conducting rigorous research and contributing new insights, ideas, and theories to the field. Our programme is built on the principles of intellectual curiosity, critical analysis, and originality, empowering you to make a significant impact in the realm of Hospitality and Tourism. Due to the programme's reputation for producing influential researchers and its strategic partnerships with leading institutions, early application is highly encouraged to secure your place in a cohort of future innovators, committed to driving positive change.

Prior Publication Mode You will need to fulfil one of the below: Obtain a master's degree in the field or related fields accepted by the HEP Senate Obtain other qualifications equivalent to a master's degree recognised by the Government of Malaysia Candidates without a related qualification in the field/s or working experience in the relevant fields must undergo appropriate prerequisite courses determined by the HEP In addition to the above criteria, those who want to join Doctoral Degree by Retrospective or Prior Publication mode must include the below to the formal application: Minimum of 5 publications or equivalent works in alignment with the theme of the specialisation; An executive summary of the above publications to demonstrate the applicant’s contribution to knowledge in the field; A list of scholarly published work; The minimum language proficiency of the candidates must be determined by the HEP consistent with applicable programme standards or based on the needs of the programme, i.e., learning outcomes and the medium of instruction. For the five (5) nominated publications or productions, the candidate must be the principal author or creator with the contributions of others clearly defined. programmes.officialAcademicRequirement: Are you ready to take the next step in your academic journey? Our programme offers an exciting opportunity for individuals passionate about the field of Bachelor of Laws. To ensure a smooth admission process, please take note of our entry requirements listed below. Prerequisites SPM / O-Level with Pre-U or Foundation Qualification Pass SPM / O-Level or equivalent with 5 credits (including English) for entry with pre-university / foundation qualification (Except for UEC) SPM / O-Level with Diploma Qualification Pass SPM / O-Level or equivalent with 3 credits (including English) for entry with Diploma qualification. Prerequisite for CLP Students who wish to pursue the CLP Examinations, will be required to show 5 credits in SPM/ equivalent in one (1) sitting, prior to joining the programme Note : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university. Entry Requirements Taylor’s Foundation* Pass with min. CGPA 2.67/4.00 Taylor’s Diploma* Pass with min. CGPA 2.67/4.00 in a related discipline Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) Pass STPM with CGPA 2.67 in 2 subjects with at least a Pass in Pengajian Am Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) A Pass in UEC with min 5Bs including English, with Max. of 20 points. For entry with UEC, the SPM prerequisites of 5 credits in one (1) sitting (prior to joining the programme), must be satisfied for students’ who wish to sit for CLP Exam. Candidates without a Grade ‘B’ in UEC English may be admitted if the candidate has a credit in English at SPM or equivalent A Level Min. CC / BD / AD AUSMAT (SACEi) Min. ATAR 70 Canadian Pre-University (CPU)* Min. average of 65% in 6 subjects International Baccalaureate (IB) 24 points in 6 subjects and at least 4 points for 3 Higher Level subjects Monash University Foundation Year (MUFY) Overall 60% Other Qualifications* Pass Foundation/ Matriculation recognised as an equivalent by the Malaysian Government / Diploma in a related discipline recognised as an equivalent by the Malaysian Government with Min CGPA of 2.67 Note : Students are advised to check with LPQB (Legal Profession Qualifying Board) on the recognition of the Pre-U programme for purposes of pursuing the CLP (Certificate of Legal Practice) All information is subject to change. The above entry requirements serve as a guideline. Readers are responsible to verify the information by contacting the university’s Admissions Department.

curriculum.en: Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to equip you with the relevant knowledge and abilities needed to thrive in the industry. By immersing yourself in a dynamic learning environment, you will gain the confidence and adaptability required to shine in different service-oriented roles.; This programme is compatible with the new Taylor's Curriculum Framework that allows students to mix & match study modules.; Click here to find out more about the Taylor's Curriculum Framework.; Primary Major; This component consists of Common Core subjects, which are common modules across a discipline that provides the fundamental knowledge of the discipline.; Core Modules; Year 1; Contract Law I; Contract Law II; Law of Tort I; Law of Tort II; Constitutional and Administrative Law I; Constitutional and Administrative Law II; English Legal System; Legal Skills and Methods; Malaysian Legal System; Year 2; Constitutional and Administrative Law III; Criminal Law I; Criminal Law II; Land Law I; Land Law II; Public International Law; Mooting; Year 3; Company Law; Equity and Trusts I; Equity and Trusts II; Family Law; Land Law III; Internship; Note; : All information is subject to change. Readers are responsible for verifying information that pertains to them by contacting the university.; University Core; This component aims to develop critical thinking, build up social intelligence and cultivate civic responsibility as well as broaden cultural knowledge. These consist of compulsory and nationally-mandated study modules required by the Malaysian Ministry of Higher Education.; Penghayatan Etika dan Peradaban / Bahasa Melayu Komunikasi 2; Falsafah dan Isu Semasa; Emotional Intelligence in Action; Kursus Integriti Dan Antirasuah; Social Innovation Project

curriculum.en: Taylor's PPE programme will take the best practices from world-renowned PPE programmes in the United Kingdom. At the same time, it will have uniquely Malaysian elements that will take advantage of the country's diverse and dynamic policy and economic landscape, in the larger context of Southeast Asia, one of the fastest-growing regions in the world. Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to equip you with the relevant knowledge and abilities needed to thrive in the industry.
